flags.name: --state-dir
flags.description: Explicit absolute owner-only OpenWiz state directory.

flags.name: --operation
flags.description: Exact 32-hex setup operation returned by the init preview.

flags.name: --help
flags.description: Print human help without sources or state; only for commands listing this flag.

flags.name: --agent
flags.description: Print this machine catalogue; only help --agent.

flags.name: --json
flags.description: Select the declared JSON success report instead of human text.

flags.name: -l
flags.description: Read reported configuration for sessions on the page; combinable with -a.

flags.name: -a
flags.description: Include archived sessions; combinable with -l.

flags.name: --hidden
flags.description: Include hidden sessions.

flags.name: --limit
flags.description: Whole number of rows, 0 through 200.

flags.name: --offset
flags.description: Whole number of matched sessions to skip.

flags.name: --yes
flags.description: Create one Cloud thread; absent means preview only.

flags.name: --dry-run
flags.description: Read and plan fleet actions only: no locks, writes, starts or messages.

flags.name: --github-only
flags.description: Read-only GitHub candidate check; required for fleet due, with no CloudRoom or state access.

flags.name: --repository
flags.description: Required GitHub repository OWNER/NAME whose App installation mints the token.

flags.name: --read
flags.description: Ask for exactly the read-only permission profile.

flags.name: --catalog
flags.description: loop validate: read every folder as a WizLoops catalog.

flags.name: --project
flags.description: loop export, plan and apply: the Cloudroom project whose loops are read and changed; required, no default.

flags.name: --out
flags.description: loop export: the folder for the exported loop files.

flags.name: --from
flags.description: loop apply: the loop file for the id; absent means ./<id>.md.

flags.name: --save
flags.description: models list: also write the offered list to docs/agents/models-offered.json beside fleet.md.

flags.name: --adopt
flags.description: loop plan and apply: bind a loop file id to an unmarked Cloudroom loop, as <id>=<loop>, for this run only.

commands.name: loop.validate

arguments.name: path
arguments.description: A loop file, or a folder of loop files, in the pinned WizLoops format.

results.when: every path read, valid or refused
usage error, or a path that cannot be read, with syntactic --json

exits.meaning: Every file valid; or help printed.
A path unreadable, or output failed; no report.
Usage error; nothing read or changed.
A file or folder refused; every refusal is reported by file and field.

rules: Exact form: loop validate <path>... [--catalog] [--json].
Checks each loop file, or each *.md file directly inside a folder except README.md, against the pinned WizLoops format (contracts/wizloops-loop.v1.md); --catalog reads every folder as a catalog.
Reads only the named files and folders and each check script they name: no room-cli, no state, no write.
Options in any order, each once; values are separate tokens that never start with -; -- ends options.

commands.name: loop.export

results.when: usage error, failed loop list or failed write with syntactic --json

exits.meaning: Every loop of the project written or unchanged; or help printed.
loop list failed, or a file or the output could not be written.
Usage error; nothing read or changed.
A loop refused; the others are still written.

rules: Exact form: loop export --project <project> [--out <dir>] [--json]. No operands.

Reads only room-cli loop list --json, keeps the loops of --project, and writes <id>.md and, for a loop with a script, <id>/check under --out (default the current directory). It never replaces a file with other bytes (export-exists) and never writes a webhook address, a secret value or a Cloudroom identifier.
Options in any order, each once; values are separate tokens that never start with -; -- ends options.

commands.name: loop.plan

arguments.name: path
arguments.description: A loop file, or a folder of loop files, in the pinned WizLoops format.

results.when: the plan was printed, with or without refusals
usage error, an unreadable path or a failed loop list, with syntactic --json

exits.meaning: Plan printed with no refusal (differences are fine) or help printed; nothing changed.
A path unreadable, loop list failed or output failed; nothing changed.
Usage error; nothing read or changed.
A file refused; the others are still planned; nothing changed.

rules: Exact form: loop plan <path>... --project <project> [--adopt <id>=<loop>]... [--json].
Reads the files and one room-cli loop list --json; prints each file's exact room-cli loop create or update and its differences; runs neither and changes nothing (contracts/loop-cli.v1.md).
Options in any order, each once except --adopt; values are separate tokens that never start with -; -- ends options.

commands.name: loop.apply

arguments.name: id
arguments.description: The one loop file id to create or update.

results.when: the loop file was read and the id planned: written, unchanged, refused, failed, different or unknown
usage error, an unreadable file, or a failed loop list before any write, with syntactic --json

exits.meaning: Created, updated or unchanged, and the read-back shows no difference; or help printed.
A read before any write failed, or output failed.
Usage error; nothing read or changed.
Refused (nothing written), failed (Cloudroom refused a command) or different (the read-back differs).
Unknown: an unclear outcome (a timeout, no exit code, or a failed read-back after a write); never retried.

rules: Exact form: loop apply <id> --project <project> [--from <path>] [--adopt <id>=<loop>] [--json]. --adopt at most once, and only for <id>. --from defaults to ./<id>.md.

Plans the one file as loop plan does, then runs only that plan's room-cli loop create or update for <id>, once, and reads the loop back with one room-cli loop list (contracts/loop-cli.v1.md). A text run prints each exact command before it runs it.

Refuses, writing nothing, a file whose id is not <id>, a file the adapter refuses, and a loop whose live item carries a setting the adapter does not map. An unclear outcome is unknown and is never retried.
Options in any order, each once; values are separate tokens that never start with -; -- ends options.

commands.name: github.token

exits.meaning: Token printed on stdout alone; its expiry on stderr.
App key or App id missing or unusable, no complete answer from GitHub, or output failure; no token.
Usage error; nothing read or minted.
No installation of this App covers the repository.
Refused: GitHub refused, or the answer granted other permissions or repositories or failed the expiry guards.

rules: Reads the key only from OPENWIZ_GITHUB_APP_KEY and the App id from OPENWIZ_GITHUB_APP_ID; authenticates as an installation, never as an App user.
Without --read exactly the App's profile; with --read exactly the read profile, for exactly that one repository.
Stores nothing: each call mints a fresh token of at most about an hour. The key and token never reach an argument, URL, log or error.
Plain text only: no --json form; stderr is one fixed sentence on failure.

commands.name: init

exits.meaning: Proposal printed, or that exact proposal applied (or already applied).
Packaged runtime, gh, a GitHub read or output unavailable.
Invalid arguments; nothing read.
Refused before private content: visibility unknown or ambiguous, unsafe, conflicting or denied companion, owner work, or closed proposal.
An effect is uncertain; apply the same operation to reconcile it against GitHub first.
The operation is unknown, refused or no longer matches GitHub; preview again.
Private setup state unavailable; nothing written.

rules: The brain follows GitHub's positively read visibility: private code in its own .openwiz/brain, public code in a private companion OWNER/NAME-brain linked back to it. No placement option or question.
Only the fixed packaged runtime beside the CLI; GitHub only through the existing gh login.

Brain records are proposed through one visible pull request; specs and tickets stay GitHub issues with the openwiz label. No credential, machine detail, runtime state or thread id enters repository content.
Every write is journalled first and read back before any retry; a repeated init reconciles existing companions, links, labels and pull requests and never overwrites owner work.

notes: Only shipped dispatch forms are listed, including fleet tick --dry-run and fleet due. The terminal app (ui) was removed in 0.0.16; no-argument openwiz prints the help in a terminal and is a usage error otherwise.
Help forms read no sources and write no state; syntactic --json wraps recognized human help, including loop-only help.
Syntactic JSON selects exactly one declared success, outcome, help or error document. Existing report shapes and numeric exit meanings are unchanged; a nonzero report remains a report.
Explicit commands remain noninteractive; no command starts a service.
Value operands and text after -- are data, never JSON selection. Existing success reports/exit meanings are preserved.
Broken stdout cannot carry a JSON error document; see the separate output-failure limitation in contracts/cli.v1.md.
Fixture proof establishes no live behaviour.
